scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: La otra banda fundadora, preferida por los estadounidenses: para Pete Fornatale fijaron los estándares que todos los que vinieron detrás deben cumplir. Jimmy Page la formó al salir de los Yardbirds con el nombre de New Yardbirds; según la leyenda, Keith Moon profetizó que caerían «como un zepelín de plomo». Page y Robert Plant son el gran ejemplo del doble foco guitarra-voz del heavy, una rivalidad afectuosa en la que ninguno eclipsa al otro, y los aullidos de Plant son uno de los modelos del canto del género. Sus temas más dulces fueron siempre carne del formato de radio hard rock.

podcast.title: Founding Lésepirín from The Jarpers' Dissolution
podcast.body: From the remnants of The Jarpers' dissolution, John Paul Jones, alongside Jimmy Page, embarked on a search for new talent, which culminated in the recruitment of Robert Plan and the subsequent formation of Lésepirín. This new band became a cornerstone of the music revolution. "Jimmy Page y a John Paul Jones que precisamente de los restos de la disolución en el amorte de los Jarpers empezarían a buscar a gente hasta que darían con Robert Plan y acabarían fondando el Ezepelín."

podcast.title: Hospitality Towards Interviewers (Mid-2000s)
podcast.body: Around 15 years prior (circa 2008), John Paul Jones of Led Zeppelin offered to make tea for an interviewer while they were preparing for an interview. This act of hospitality highlights a pattern among "bigger" artists. "About 15 years ago, John Paul Jones of Led Zeppelin offered to make me tea while I was getting ready for an interview."

podcast.title: Member of The Jarpers and Lésepirín Founder
podcast.body: John Paul Jones was also a member of The Jarpers, a group that saw many incredible guitarists pass through its ranks. After The Jarpers' demise, he joined Jimmy Page in forming Lésepirín, becoming a pivotal figure in one of rock's most influential bands. "También estuvo encima John Paul Jones también de los lésepirín como un grupo en el que pasaron tantos guitarristas increíbles no terminó de coajar."

podcast.title: Producer Role for Butthole Surfers
podcast.body: John Paul Jones, widely recognized as the bass player for Led Zeppelin, also took on a producing role for the Butthole Surfers. He produced their 1993 track, "The Annoying Song," from the album "Independent Worms Saloon." "By the way, that song was produced by John Paul Jones, the bass player for Let's Set Plane."

xref.title: One-Night-Only Reunion (2007)
xref.body: Led Zeppelin reunited for a single, historic concert at the O2 in London on December 10, 2007. This event was prompted by the death of Ahmet Ertegun, the founder of Atlantic Records, who had signed the band in the late 1960s and was crucial to their rise. The lineup included Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, and John Paul Jones, with John's son, Jason Bonham, filling in on drums for his late father. It was the first significant appearance for Led Zeppelin in 27 years, attracting an overwhelming 20 million ticket applications. The band performed a 16-song set that night, but despite the massive success and acclaim, they have not played together again since. "On December 10th, 2007, Led Zeppelin reunited for a one night only concert at the O2 in London."

xref.body: The three members of Them Crooked Vultures—Dave Grohl, Josh Homme, and John Paul Jones—are collectively responsible for selling an estimated 150 million to 200 million albums throughout their careers. "In that semi-circle, there were people responsible for selling, what, 150 million albums, 200 million albums?"

xref.title: Interview at Pink Duck Studios, Burbank
xref.body: The band was interviewed at Josh Homme's Pink Duck Studios in Burbank, which from the front resembled an old corner store with a blocked door, but around back offered access to a small parking area with a deck and picnic table. The interview included Josh Homme, John Paul Jones, and Dave Grohl. "One Wednesday, I got a call asking if I'd like to interview the band in Josh's studio in Burbank."

xref.title: John Paul Jones's Courtesy
xref.body: John Paul Jones, the bassist for Led Zeppelin and member of Them Crooked Vultures, demonstrated exceptional politeness during an interview at Pink Duck Studios. He offered to fetch tea and returned with it promptly, even plucking some "vaguely Zeppelin-esque notes" on a bass before doing so. "Splendid. Just ask if you need anything. Can I get you a cup of tea?"

xref.title: John Paul Jones's Tea Service
xref.body: During an interview at Pink Duck Studios, John Paul Jones, the legendary bassist from Led Zeppelin, offered and fetched a cup of tea for an interviewer. He inquired about preference for milk or lemon and returned promptly with a cup and saucer. "Did I just send the bass player a Led Zeppelin out to fetch me a cup of tea?"

xref.title: Supergroup Formation
xref.body: Them Crooked Vultures was formed as a supergroup, bringing together Josh Homme, Foo Fighters' Dave Grohl, and Led Zeppelin's bass player John Paul Jones. "Josh was one-third of them crooked vultures, a supergroup that featured Buddy Dave Grohl and Led Zeppelin bass player John Paul Jones."

xref.title: Supergroup Formation (Years Ago)
xref.body: The band formed after years of casual discussions among Dave Grohl (Foo Fighters), Josh Homme (Queens of the Stone Age), and John Paul Jones (Led Zeppelin) about creating music together. They finally decided to make it a reality. "After years of joking about forming a band together, Dave Grohl of the Fung Fighters, Josh Hommie of Queens of the Stone Age, and Led Zeppelin's John Paul Jones decided to make it happen with them crooked vultures."
